doc.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Max Roach's melodic drumming
summary: Roach made drums a musical instrument.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Max Roach. Somewhere in the late ’50s, early ’60s, that’s a part of your musical experience. Can you speak to that?

Max was – I’m surprised that the other drummers didn’t hear what Max was doing, because he started making the drums a real musical instrument, especially when you played a solo. That solo had to be musical. You couldn’t just play the rudiments or play some fast rolls or something like that. You had to make some music. I was surprised that the drummers didn’t more so – they weren’t more so influenced by that. Because there are some other guys that had a better feeling with the cymbal than Max when he’s playing swing, but in the solos, he was the man. Those solos made a hell of a lot of sense. They were like an instrument – like a wind instrument playing a melody.
